problem_markdown: Define $f(1)=1$, $f(3)=3$, $f(2n)=f(n)$, $f(4n+1)=2f(2n+1)-f(n)$, and $f(4n+3)=3f(2n+1)-2f(n)$ for positive integers $n$. How many $n\le1988$ satisfy $f(n)=n$?
solutions_markdown:
Let $R(n)$ be the integer obtained by reversing the binary digits of $n$, discarding leading zeros. Then $R(2n)=R(n)$. If $n$ has $\ell$ binary digits, $R(2n+1)=2^\ell+R(n)$. Consequently
$$R(4n+1)=2^{\ell+1}+R(n)=2R(2n+1)-R(n),$$
$$R(4n+3)=2^{\ell+1}+R(2n+1)=3R(2n+1)-2R(n).$$
Together with $R(1)=1,R(3)=3$, these prove by induction that $f=R$.

The fixed points are therefore exactly the binary palindromes. With $L$ digits their count is $2^{\lceil L/2\rceil-1}$: the first digit is one and the remaining first-half digits determine the rest. For lengths 1 through 10 the counts sum to $1+1+2+2+4+4+8+8+16+16=62$. There are 32 eleven-digit palindromes up to 2047, and exactly two exceed 1988: $2015=(11111011111)_2$ and $2047=(11111111111)_2$. Hence the answer is $62+30=92$.
